requirements.statement: When adding a transporter was started from the address book, the 'Choose a transporter type' Back link goes to the address book's 'Choose an address type' question, and the ordinary add-address form opened while Transporter is the chosen address type sends the trader back to that question.
requirements.why: The add pages are the address book's, reached from its own address type question as well as from the journey, and the 6 November ruling gives the Transporter option on that question somewhere to lead.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-015 and repo-tests-p15-008 return the Back link to the address type question, repo-insfrontend-p7-105 proves it in the fit suite, and repo-tests-p15-009 sends the ordinary add form back to the question while Transporter is chosen.

requirements.statement: When adding a transporter was started from the address book, saving adds it to the organisation's transporters in the address book, shows the address book's success banner '<name> added to your address book', and goes to the address book filtered to transporters, where it is listed with its type, address and approval number and found by a search on its name, type, address, approval number or country.
requirements.why: A transporter added from the address book should be there straight away, and the address book is the system of record for transporters.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-049, repo-tests-p15-026 and -027 land the trader on the address book filtered to transporters under a success banner naming the record; repo-tests-p15-029, -031, -039, -040, -042 and -043 and repo-insfrontend-p7-110, -114, -119 and -121 prove the listing and the search, with and without JavaScript.

requirements.statement: A transporter is a record the address book service holds for one organisation, in its own transporters collection with its own document, controller, repository and route, reusing the service's organisation scoping, soft-delete status, optimistic locking and Standard Address Block field validation where the fields are genuinely the same; the address book is the system of record for transporters.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling settles the question the 9 October afternoon ruling left blocked: the address book manages transporters, saved per organisation exactly as every other address is, and it does so in a collection of its own rather than on the Address model. The ruling leaves the full field list to the service, which keeps the Standard Address Block fields with a phone and an email.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-001 and -002 hold transporters in their own transporters collection on their own route, repo-addressbook-p4-003 gives the record the Standard Address Block fields with phone, email, type and approval number, repo-addressbook-p4-005 locks it optimistically, and repo-tests-p15-052 proves a transporter can be created straight through the address book API.

requirements.statement: A transporter holds no address role and no address type, no seventh address role and no fourth role group is added for it, and the address book's address API is unchanged by transporters: a transporter request carrying roles or a role is refused on that field.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling: an address role says which records a notification's picker may offer for a slot, drives the receiving-roles-in-the-United-Kingdom rule and drives the address list's category tabs, and a transporter is none of the six roles and has one use, so a role would carry no information for it. The address book's own request shapes could not hold a transporter in any case: they require at least one role and refuse a type outright.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-025 and -026 refuse roles and role on a transporter request, repo-addressbook-p4-040 returns a transporter with no roles and no address type, and repo-tests-p15-012 holds a transporter's type as one of two values.

requirements.statement: A transporter record carries a required private-or-commercial type, PRIVATE or COMMERCIAL, stored on the record rather than worked out from anything else; a commercial transporter must have an approval number and a private one must not, a blank approval number counting as none; no address carries either.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling: a transporter's type is intrinsic because it decides the form, the field list and the country rule, so unlike an address's type it cannot be derived. The approval status the same ruling names is its own requirement (req-2263), because the address book does not hold one yet.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-023, -029 and -030 require the type and refuse any other value, repo-addressbook-p4-031 to -033 hold the approval number rules, repo-insfrontend-p7-038 and -038-m1 never ask or save one for a private transporter, and repo-tests-p15-028 and -038 store the type with the approval number only for a commercial one. repo-addressbook-p4-094 shows no approval status on the record today, which req-2263 adds.

requirements.statement: 'Add a transporter' on the transporter list opens the address book's add-a-transporter pages in journey mode, with the controls the address add pages show in journey mode, and lands the trader back on the transporter list on save or on cancel, through the same hand-off the journey already uses to add an address; the animals frontend serves no transporter add pages of its own.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling makes the address book the system of record and has a journey that needs a new transporter open the INS front door's add pages in journey mode, using the hand-off already built for addresses rather than a second pattern of its own, with those pages living in the front door rather than in the animals frontend's three transporter add-page folders. Keeping those folders would be the second pattern it refuses, so their routes, fit specs and copy keys go with them; both journey details pages are signed off, so the change goes through the signed-off check. The address book's own transporter pages are all still exploring, so changing them trips no signed-off check.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's add pages always return to the address book filtered to transporters, on save (repo-insfrontend-p7-049, repo-tests-p15-026) and on cancel (repo-insfrontend-p7-045), with no journey return, and the animals frontend still serves its own type question and two details forms inside the journey. The address book's pages are at maturity 'exploring' (repo-insfrontend-p7-001).

requirements.statement: A transporter row's only actions are the radio that picks the transporter and the 'View details' link: a transporter is changed or deleted from its own page in the address book, which offers Edit and Delete and a Back link to the address book filtered to transporters.
requirements.why: The journey picks a transporter; managing the record belongs with the service that holds it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-060, repo-tests-p15-049 and -050 put Edit and Delete and the Back link on the transporter's own page in the address book; the journey list's row actions are recorded by the transporters area.

requirements.statement: An organisation's transporters are the records the address book holds for it: no transporter captured before the address book became their system of record is carried over.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling leaves open what becomes of transporter records captured before the change, and there are none to carry over: the store it replaced kept them in one process's memory, so they were lost on every restart, and the records a trader adds already go to the address book.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-047 creates each transporter as a record in the address book and repo-tests-p15-052 proves the address book holds it, so nothing is left elsewhere to carry over.

requirements.statement: A commercial transporter's country is stored as the Northern Ireland country code the address book already uses and shown as 'Northern Ireland' by both the address book and the journey.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling forces a created commercial transporter to a Northern Ireland country code rather than looking one up, and keeps the code and its display name as constants in the service. Which code that is settles how the value is held rather than anything a trader sees, so the service's own choice stands unless the owner means the literal code the ruling names (c-388).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-063 and repo-insfrontend-p7-003 store the fixed country as the code GB-NIR, and repo-insfrontend-p7-059 and repo-tests-p15-036 show it as the words 'Northern Ireland'.

requirements.statement: The address book refuses a commercial transporter whose country is not Northern Ireland with 'A commercial transporter must be in Northern Ireland', and the address book's commercial add and edit forms refuse a posted country other than Northern Ireland with the same message, always saving a commercial transporter with the Northern Ireland code.
requirements.why: The address book is the system of record for transporters, so a transporter written straight through its API cannot escape the rule; the 6 November ruling names the add form's hidden field and its refusal of a tampered value, and the service's own refusal on write stands beside it as a real validation constraint (c-389).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-034 refuses a commercial transporter whose country code is not GB-NIR with that message, as an exact match (repo-addressbook-p4-035), keyed by the field (repo-addressbook-p4-037); repo-insfrontend-p7-041 and -072 refuse a tampered post on the add and edit forms and repo-insfrontend-p7-042 always saves GB-NIR.

requirements.statement: The transporters route the address book serves is designed in the address book's own conventions: its paths, its pages, its soft-delete and its paging, which takes a 1-based page defaulting to 1 and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, as the address list's does, and answers an object of items, page, page size, total items and total pages; an out-of-range or non-numeric page or page size is a 400 bad-request problem.
requirements.why: The prototype never decides a service's paths, field names or API, and the 6 November ruling gives the transporter its own controller, repository and route without saying what the surface is, leaving it to the service. The 25 November and 5 November rulings fix the paging bounds for every list the address book serves.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-046, -047, -049, -051 and -055 serve list, create, get, replace and delete under /organisation/{orgId}/transporters, and repo-addressbook-p4-065 to -067 page it with the address list's bounds.

requirements.statement: The address book sets a transporter's id, its organisation (from the caller's identity header), its live status and its created and modified times itself; any of them sent in a request body is accepted and ignored.
requirements.why: The system of record owns its server fields, so no caller can place a transporter in another organisation or back-date it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-004, -027 and -061 set the server fields and ignore those sent, proven by the service's create tests.

requirements.statement: The address book refuses, as a 400 validation problem keyed by the field, a transporter whose name or address line 1 is blank or over 255 characters, whose address line 2 is over 255, whose town or city is blank or over 100, whose county is over 100, whose postcode is blank or over 12, whose country code is blank, whose phone is blank or over 20, whose email is blank, malformed or over 254, or whose approval number is over 50; the postcode, phone and approval number are checked for presence and length only, and the country code is stored as given.
requirements.why: The address book is the system of record, so its own rules hold for a transporter however it is written; they are the Standard Address Block's limits the 6 November ruling reuses.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-007 to -024 hold every rule, proven by the request validation tests, and repo-tests-p15-041 stores an NI/TA approval number unchanged.

requirements.statement: A transporter the address book returns carries, in camelCase, its id, name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode, country code, phone, email, type, approval number, organisation id, a deleted flag and its created and modified times, with an unset address line 2, county or approval number written as null; it never carries roles, an address type, the internal soft-delete status, its expiry date or its version.
requirements.why: Every consumer reads one shape, and soft deletion is shown only as a deleted flag so the internal tombstone status can change without breaking a caller.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-039 and -041 to -044-m1 give the response's fields, proven by the mapper and response tests.

requirements.statement: The address book's transporter list holds only the caller's organisation's live transporters, newest first by creation time and then by id; a soft-deleted transporter leaves the list.
requirements.why: The list is what every picker and the Transporter tab read, so it shows what the organisation holds now, most recent first.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-068 and -069 order and filter the list, proven by the service and delete tests.

requirements.statement: The transporter list's search term is trimmed and matched as literal text, ignoring case, against any part of a transporter's name, address lines, town or city, county, postcode or approval number, never its country code, phone, email or type; repeatable country codes and search types match a transporter in any given country or of any given type; a transporter matching the term, a country or a search type is listed; and an absent or blank term, country code or search type adds nothing, repeats counting once.
requirements.why: The Transporter tab's single search box finds a transporter by its name, address, approval number, country name or type word, which the front door turns into the term, country codes and search types.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-070 to -075 and -078 hold the search, proven by the transporter search tests.

requirements.statement: A repeatable type filter on the transporter list keeps only transporters of the given types across every page and narrows the search; an unknown type or search type value is a 400 bad-request problem with no errors map.
requirements.why: The Transporter tab's Type filter narrows the whole tab on the server rather than one page of it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-076 and -077 are proven by the transporter search tests.

requirements.statement: Reading a transporter by id returns it to its own organisation, a soft-deleted one included and marked deleted; an unknown id and another organisation's id both answer the same 404 'Transporter not found', so the service never confirms that another organisation holds an id.
requirements.why: A notification can still show a transporter that was later deleted, and nothing leaks another organisation's records.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-049, -050 and -083 are proven by the service, delete and scoping tests.

requirements.statement: Replacing a live transporter replaces every field the caller sends, clearing an optional field left out, keeps its id, organisation, status, created time and expiry date, and moves its modified time on; replacing a soft-deleted, unknown or another organisation's transporter answers 404, and a save from a stale copy is refused as a 409 conflict rather than overwriting a later change.
requirements.why: Optimistic locking keeps two editors, or a late write after a delete, from silently overwriting each other.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-051 to -054 and -005 hold the replace and the lock; the 409 is documented but not driven by a test (repo-addressbook-p4-006). The API lets a replace change the type (repo-addressbook-p4-053), which the front door's edit form never sends.

requirements.statement: Deleting a transporter soft-deletes it and answers 204 with no body: its status becomes deleted, its modified time moves on and its approval number stays; deleting it again answers 204 and changes nothing, and deleting an unknown id answers a 404 not-found problem.
requirements.why: The address book's soft-delete rule holds for transporters exactly as for addresses, so a submitted notification's transporter stays readable.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-055 to -060 are proven by the transporter delete tests.

requirements.statement: Every transporter operation needs the trusted organisation id header and is authorised against the path organisation: a missing header is a 400, a header that disagrees with the path answers 404 and changes nothing, and one organisation never lists or reaches another's transporters.
requirements.why: Transporters belong to an organisation, as addresses do, and the 6 November ruling reuses the address book's organisation scoping for them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-080 to -082 are proven by the scoping tests, and repo-tests-p15-030 shows another organisation's address book holding none of them.

requirements.statement: The transporters collection has one index besides its id, on organisation, status and creation time, and the live list query uses it rather than scanning the collection.
requirements.why: Organisations in test environments hold thousands of records, so the list stays fast as the collection grows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-085 is proven by the transporter index test.

requirements.statement: Outside prod, when a time to live is configured, a new transporter expires that many days after it is created, and a later update or soft delete keeps that date; in prod transporters and their tombstones are kept indefinitely.
requirements.why: The address book's expiry rule holds for transporters exactly as for addresses, so test environments do not fill up.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-086 and -088 hold the rule, reusing the address time-to-live setting.

requirements.statement: Each transporter operation, and the list's database query, is timed as a metric, and the list logs whether a search term was given, never its text, with the page, page size, country codes and types.
requirements.why: The transporters route is observed like the address routes without logging what a trader searched for.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-089 and -090 name the metrics and the log line.

requirements.statement: The address book's OpenAPI contract documents the five transporter operations under a transporters tag, 'An organisation's transporters, scoped to its address book', with name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, country code, phone, email and type as the request's required fields.
requirements.why: Callers of the system of record build against its published contract.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-091 and -093 are in the locked contract.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: minor inconsistencies in the address book's transporter validation and contract that no trader sees, namely the generated contract giving required string fields a minimum length of 0, a request with no type and an approval number also being refused as private, and a blank commercial country getting two messages on one field.
requirements.why: None of them reaches a trader through the front door's forms, which validate first, and none changes what is stored; they go to the report rather than into an increment.

requirements.statement: Choosing Transporter on the address book's 'Choose an address type' question opens the transporter type question afresh, clearing any transporter part-way through being added.
requirements.why: Starting again from the address type question should never carry over half-entered details from an earlier attempt.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-005 and -006 open the question at its start and clear the in-progress entry, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-106 and repo-tests-p15-001.

requirements.statement: The address book's 'Choose a transporter type' page has the caption 'Add a new transporter', the heading and title 'Choose a transporter type', the warning text 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.', a visually hidden legend 'Choose a transporter type', the radios 'Private transporter' with no hint then 'Commercial' with the hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.', and one 'Continue' button.
requirements.why: The address book's type question is the one route to adding a transporter, and it already reads as the journey's type question does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-007 to -014 hold the copy and repo-tests-p15-002 to -007 prove it end to end.

requirements.statement: Continuing on the address book's 'Choose a transporter type' with no option chosen re-shows it with status 400 and the error 'Select a transporter type', inline against the radios and in a 'There is a problem' summary whose link moves focus to 'Private transporter', with and without JavaScript.
requirements.why: The address book's type question becomes the one route (req-2264), so it takes the design's refusal wording that the journey's own question carries today; this is the same change as req-420 on the page that remains.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's question refuses with 'Select what kind of transporter it is' (repo-insfrontend-p7-016, repo-tests-p15-010); the status, summary and focus already match.

requirements.statement: On the address book's type question, 'Private transporter' opens 'Add a private transporter' and 'Commercial' opens 'Add a commercial transporter'; the chosen type is remembered so the question shows it chosen on return, and values already typed on a form are kept when the type is changed.
requirements.why: A trader who goes back to change the type should not lose what they have typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-017, -017-m1 and -018 hold the routing and memory, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-108 and repo-tests-p15-013 and -032.

requirements.statement: Opening or posting the address book's private or commercial add form with no transporter type chosen, or a different one, sends the trader to 'Choose a transporter type' and saves nothing.
requirements.why: The form a trader fills in must match the type they chose, because the type decides the fields and the country rule.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-020 guards both forms, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-112 and -117 and repo-tests-p15-022.

requirements.statement: The address book's add forms carry the caption 'Add a new transporter' and the heading and title 'Add a private transporter' or 'Add a commercial transporter'.
requirements.why: The address book's add forms are the one route and already read as the journey's do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-021 to -023 hold the copy, proven by repo-tests-p15-014, -015 and -033, and the private form's opening in the cross-browser and iOS runs too (repo-tests-p15-135).

requirements.statement: The address book's add and edit forms ask, in order, the name, the approval number on a commercial form only, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address, and Phone number with the hint 'For international numbers include the country code'; the name and address line 1 are required and at most 255 characters, address line 2 at most 255, town or city required and at most 100, county at most 100, postcode required and at most 12, email required and at most 254, phone required and at most 20, and the approval number required and at most 50; every value is trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is checked and saved.
requirements.why: The forms ask the Standard Address Block's fields and contact fields with its limits, as the 11 November ruling settles; the name and approval number labels and the section headings are their own requirements (req-2265, req-2266, req-2267).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-025 to -035 and -039 hold the fields, their order, the phone hint, the limits and the trimming; repo-tests-p15-017 and -018 prove the fields end to end. Today the name reads 'Name or organisation', the approval number 'Approval number' and the fields sit under 'Address' and 'Contact details' (repo-insfrontend-p7-024, repo-tests-p15-016), which the label and heading requirements change.

requirements.statement: The address book's transporter form fields carry the browser autocomplete hints address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, postal-code, email and tel, with town, county, postcode and country at half width and phone at two-thirds width.
requirements.why: Autocomplete hints help every trader and are a WCAG input-purpose requirement; the widths follow GOV.UK guidance for the expected length.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-034 sets the hints and widths.

requirements.statement: A blank name on the address book's transporter forms shows 'Enter a name or organisation name'.
requirements.why: The address book's forms are the one route, so they take the design's message that the journey's own form carries; this is the same change as req-435's name message on the page that remains.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's forms show 'Enter a name or organisation' (repo-insfrontend-p7-025), and no message is proven end to end on them (repo-tests-p15-054).

requirements.statement: On the address book's transporter forms a blank required field other than the name shows its own message: 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address', 'Enter a phone number', 'Select a country' for a private transporter, and 'Enter the approval number' for a commercial one, each inline and in the error summary.
requirements.why: Each field says what is missing, as the journey's forms do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-026 to -039 hold each message and repo-insfrontend-p7-120 proves the approval number one; the rest are not yet proven end to end (repo-tests-p15-054).

requirements.statement: An over-long value on the address book's transporter forms is refused with '<field> must be <n> characters or less', using the field's label, and the typed value is kept.
requirements.why: The address book's forms are the one route, so they take the design's length message the journey's own forms carry; this is the same change as req-436 on the pages that remain, and the address book's own refusals already end 'or less'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's forms end each length message 'characters or fewer' and name the field by a short name such as 'Name' or 'Postcode' (repo-insfrontend-p7-025 to -039); no length limit is proven end to end on them (repo-tests-p15-055).

requirements.statement: A malformed email address on the address book's transporter forms is refused with 'Enter an email address in the correct format', and the address book refuses one on write.
requirements.why: The address book, the system of record, refuses a malformed email on write, which is a real validation constraint; a form that let one through would only fail at the service. This departs from req-439's 'presence and length only' for the email address, which the cross-area pass should reconcile.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-031 and repo-addressbook-p4-021 both refuse a malformed email with that message.

requirements.statement: The private transporter's Country select on the address book's add and edit forms is a plain select that opens with United Kingdom chosen when no country is held, with no 'Select a country' placeholder.
requirements.why: The address book's form is the one route, so it takes the design's select the journey's own form carries; this is the same change as req-431 on the page that remains, and a field the prototype shows as a plain select stays one.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's private form opens the select on the placeholder 'Select a country' (repo-insfrontend-p7-036), and its edit form shows the placeholder first when the stored country is not offered (repo-insfrontend-p7-068-m1); no test asserts which countries it holds or where they come from (repo-tests-p15-056, -057).

requirements.statement: A posted country that is not on the private transporter form's list is refused with 'Select a country from the list', with the select cleared.
requirements.why: A tampered or stale value tells the trader to pick from the list rather than that nothing was picked; this is req-433's message on the page that remains.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's private form answers a country not on the list with 'Select a country', the same as a missing one (repo-insfrontend-p7-037).

requirements.statement: Editing a private transporter whose saved country is no longer offered opens the form with 'The saved country is no longer available. Select a country from the list.'
requirements.why: The trader is told why the country needs choosing again; this is req-433's message on the page that remains.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's edit form shows the 'Select a country' placeholder first with no message when the stored country is not offered (repo-insfrontend-p7-068-m1).

requirements.statement: On the address book's commercial transporter form the country is fixed: a disabled 'Country' select shows 'Northern Ireland' and cannot be changed, and a hidden field posts it.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling makes a commercial transporter's country a fixed value, not a choice, posted in a hidden field with no reference-data lookup.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-040 holds the disabled select and hidden field, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-116 and repo-tests-p15-035.

requirements.statement: Started from the address book, both add forms end with a 'Save and continue' button and a secondary 'Cancel and return to address book' button, which forgets the transporter being added and returns to the address book filtered to transporters, creating nothing.
requirements.why: A trader who started in the address book goes back there when they give up.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-044 and -045 hold the buttons and the cancel, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-113 and -118 and repo-tests-p15-023 to -025.

requirements.statement: Both add forms' Back links go to 'Choose a transporter type' with the chosen type still chosen, and what the trader typed is shown again when a form is reopened, until the transporter is saved or cancelled.
requirements.why: Going back never loses the trader's answers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-046 and -047 hold the Back link and the kept values, proven by repo-tests-p15-021 and -037.

requirements.statement: A transporter add or edit form that fails validation, or that the address book refuses as invalid, is shown again with status 400, the entered values kept and each error inline and in the error summary; any other failure to save shows the form again with its values and a recoverable error, with status 500.
requirements.why: The trader can always correct and resubmit, and the address book's own refusals reach the field they concern.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-048, -050, -051 and -075 hold the three outcomes on add and edit.

requirements.statement: A transporter's own page in the address book, reached from 'View <name>' on the Transporter tab, is headed and titled with its name and lists, in order, its name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode, country by name ('Northern Ireland' for a commercial one), approval number, type ('Private' or 'Commercial'), email and phone, leaving out address line 2 and county when empty and the approval number for a private transporter; it has a secondary 'Edit' button and a warning 'Delete' button.
requirements.why: The address book is where a transporter is looked at and managed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-052 to -060 hold the page, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-122 to -124 and repo-tests-p15-044 to -049; its rows use the forms' field labels (repo-insfrontend-p7-055).

requirements.statement: A transporter's own page carries the return destination it was opened with onto its Edit and Delete links, and its Back link goes to that destination, or to the address book filtered to transporters when there is none.
requirements.why: A trader who opened the transporter from a journey can get back to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-061 honours the return, and repo-insfrontend-p7-125 and repo-tests-p15-050 prove the default Back link.

requirements.statement: Opening a transporter's own page, edit page or delete page for a transporter that is deleted, not found or addressed by an id that is not a record id sends the trader to the return destination or the Transporter tab and logs it; failing to load the transporter shows the error page.
requirements.why: An old or mistyped link never shows a broken page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-062 to -064 hold the redirects and the error page.

requirements.statement: A transporter's edit page, 'Edit transporter details', opens holding its stored values in the form of its stored type, which cannot be changed, with the same labels, hint and checks as that type's add form; 'Save changes' updates it and shows '<name> updated in your address book', and the secondary 'Cancel' and the Back link return to the transporter's own page saving nothing; saving a transporter that is no longer live sends the trader to the return destination or the Transporter tab.
requirements.why: A transporter's type decides its fields and country rule, so an edit keeps it; changing type means adding a new transporter.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-065 to -074 hold the edit page, proven for a private transporter by repo-insfrontend-p7-126 to -129.

requirements.statement: After saving an edit or confirming a delete, the trader lands on the return destination the transporter's page was opened with, unless it is one of that transporter's own pages, and otherwise on the address book filtered to transporters.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses rather than a second pattern, and the address pages already land on their return destination after a delete (req-1167); the transporter's page already carries the destination onto Edit and Delete, so dropping it after the save strands a trader who came from a journey.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a saved edit and a confirmed delete always land on the Transporter tab, whatever return destination the pages carried (repo-insfrontend-p7-073-m1).

requirements.statement: A transporter's delete page, 'Delete this transporter?', summarises it in one 'Transporter' row of its name, address lines and country name, one per line, and says 'Confirm that you want to delete this transporter.' and 'Deletions are permanent and you cannot undo this.'; a warning 'Yes, delete' button deletes it and shows '<name> deleted from your address book', or 'Transporter deleted from your address book' when it has no name, and a 'No, cancel' link and the Back link return to its own page; confirming the delete of a transporter that is no longer live sends the trader to the return destination or the Transporter tab, and any other failure shows the error page.
requirements.why: Deleting is confirmed on a page rather than a pop-up, as every confirmation in the service is.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-076 to -082 hold the delete page, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-131 to -133.

requirements.statement: The INS front door reads and writes transporters only through the address book's organisation-scoped transporters resource, listing with page, page size and optional types, search term, country codes and search types, and reading the address book's field-level refusals on create and update so they show on the form.
requirements.why: The address book is the system of record, so the front door keeps no transporter store of its own outside stub mode.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-083 to -085 hold the client.

requirements.statement: In stub mode the INS front door keeps transporters in an in-memory store per organisation that applies the address book's approval number and commercial country rules, its search and type filtering, its newest-first order and paging, and its soft delete.
requirements.why: The front door's fit suite runs without the address book and must see the same rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-086 to -094 mirror the service's rules; the stub merges an update into the stored record where the service replaces it (repo-insfrontend-p7-095), which no form shows because the edit form always sends every field.

requirements.statement: Saving a transporter does not check for or refuse a duplicate; the type question's warning to check the transporter list first is the only guard.
requirements.why: No source asks for a duplicate check, and the design's warning asks the trader to look first.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-096: nothing on the forms or in the stub refuses a duplicate.

requirements.statement: The address book's transporter type, add and edit pages are sent with Cache-Control: no-store.
requirements.why: The browser keeps no copy of pages holding a trader's contact details.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-019 sets the header on each controller.

requirements.statement: Every English string on the address book's transporter pages has a Welsh counterpart in the address book's Welsh copy, which stays a machine draft that is not shown to users until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The front door is bilingual, and unreviewed Welsh must not reach users.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-098 to -104 hold the Welsh for every transporter page, marked a machine draft by repo-insfrontend-p7-097.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the warning icon's screen-reader fallback 'Warning' on the transporter type question is written in English in the template rather than taken from the copy file, so the Welsh page reads it in English.
requirements.why: The Welsh copy is an unreviewed machine draft that does not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off, and the fix belongs with that review rather than this programme; it goes to the report.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: gaps in today's end-to-end proof of transporter management that no requirement changes, namely editing and deleting a transporter through the tests repo and editing a commercial transporter in the front door's fit suite.
requirements.why: The behaviour exists and is proven for a private transporter in the front door's fit suite; closing proof gaps the programme does not touch goes to the report, as the other proof gaps do. Pages a requirement changes are proven when that requirement is built.

conflicts.about: Which Northern Ireland country code a commercial transporter is stored with: the code the 6 November ruling names, or the one the address book already uses.

positions.says: The country code persisted for a commercial transporter is XI, displayed as 'Northern Ireland', with both held as constants in the service.
The question put was whether MDM is used for a Northern Ireland country lookup or a created commercial transporter is simply forced to a Northern Ireland country code.
A commercial transporter's country code must be exactly GB-NIR, and any other value is refused.
Northern Ireland is stored as the country code GB-NIR.
A commercial transporter's fixed country is stored as the code GB-NIR and shown as the words 'Northern Ireland' by both the address book and the journey.

conflicts.outcome: The 6 November ruling can be read two ways and nothing ranks them. Read as a value, it names XI and justifies it against the estate's own schemas, so the address book's constant, its exact-match check, the front door's constant and hidden field and the records already stored with GB-NIR all change. Read as a decision between an MDM lookup and a forced code, which is how the question was put to the owner, it settles only that the code is forced, and which code the service holds is how the shape is held in code, the real service's own call, which it has already made as GB-NIR in both the address book and the front door. The two readings build different things in two services, and no trader sees either code, both being shown as the words 'Northern Ireland'.
conflicts.question: Is a commercial transporter's country stored as the literal code XI, or as the Northern Ireland country code the address book already uses?
conflicts.default: Keep what is built: the address book and the INS front door store and check the fixed country as GB-NIR, and both show it as 'Northern Ireland' (req-2275). Nothing is rewritten. The rule that a commercial transporter must be in Northern Ireland stays enforceable from the stored value alone either way, because the code is distinct from the United Kingdom's (req-2276).

conflicts.about: Which service refuses a commercial transporter whose country is not Northern Ireland.

positions.says: The commercial transporter add form refuses a tampered country value rather than correcting it.
The ruling does not say whether the forced Northern Ireland country is enforced by the address book service as well as by the add form.
The address book refuses a commercial transporter whose country code is not Northern Ireland's with 'A commercial transporter must be in Northern Ireland'.
The front door's commercial form refuses a posted country other than Northern Ireland with the same message.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and what it says stands: the add form refuses a tampered country value. It is silent on the service, and the address book, the system of record, already refuses a commercial transporter outside Northern Ireland on write, a real validation constraint the ruling does not set aside, so both guards are kept and both are already built (req-2277). The earlier doubt rested on the service possibly lacking the check; the address book's own code and tests now show it there. Nothing is overruled: the ruling's claims still carry the form's refusal, and the repo claims are the evidence that both exist.
